prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, from the magic-wavelength trapping concept to atomic timekeeping at the 10^-18 level.

statement.case_for: I keep the optical lattice clock as my single-part preference and I have not changed my configuration since round 1. The scientific case has not been challenged by anyone: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes the light shift so that many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, and Ye's group, among others, took the systematic uncertainty to about 1e-18. The performance is reproduced in strontium and ytterbium in several national laboratories, and it is used for geodesy, for bounds on drifting constants and for the evidence base of a redefined second, so maturity is secure whether or not the redefinition happens before the decision. The round-1 exchange confirmed what mattered most to me: B013 is the only entry whose two-name allocation is described the same way by members from every camp, and the chair's summary shows that even the Higgs supporters regard it as a legitimate fallback. For the citation I would name the lattice idea and the 1e-18 realization, not the frequency comb and not precision optical clocks in general, which keeps it distinct from 2005 and 2012 and does not claim that lattice clocks are the only route to this accuracy.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize is real, and a sceptic can call this a refinement of a lineage already well honoured. Credit for the early demonstrations and the comparison campaigns extends beyond two names (Lemonde and the Paris group, Takamoto, the PTB groups and the JILA team members), and the redefinition of the second is still pending. Against my own choice, the Higgs discovery is the larger result for physics and its experimental half has been unrecognised since 2013. If the committee could settle three Higgs names by a rule that does not depend on whose recollection one trusts, I would take that case seriously, and a prize that passes over it will look narrow to many outside metrology.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, argues that the Higgs discovery is mature and unrecognised, that the attribution difficulty is a judgement on leadership, and that Virdee and Della Negra are nearly interchangeable on the supplied evidence; the chair summary also asks whether a principle can select three of the four credited names.
responses.response: I accept the maturity argument without reservation, and I accept that the discovery will not be revised. My difficulty is with the word interchangeable. If two of four named founders are interchangeable, then the choice between them is not made by the evidence, and the three supporters have in fact produced two different trios (Pearce and Danielsson with Virdee, Johansson with Della Negra). A principle such as founding conception versus spokesperson at the time of the announcement would decide the seat, but it would also apply separately to ATLAS and to CMS and does not itself limit the count to three. Until the supporters agree on one trio and one rule, I cannot rank the Higgs above a configuration where nobody has to justify an omission. I would not oppose a Higgs prize if the supporters converge, and I keep it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Johansson prefers the Higgs discovery, with Gianotti, Della Negra and Jenni, treats attribution as a reason to choose names carefully rather than to defer, and states that B013 is a serious fallback rather than a token one.
responses.response: I share his view that attribution should be handled by careful choice and not used as an excuse for postponement, and I note that my own opening ballot proposed the same trio as his. That is the difficulty: after reading round 1 I see that three members of the room have remembered three different trios for the same entry, and each one honestly describes his recollection of spokesperson terms and conception as unverified. I take his fallback statement at face value, and it is the reason I see no real conflict between us. If the committee prefers significance, he and Pearce should tell us which three names they would sign, and I will weigh that against the clean allocation of B013. I also note his wish that B054 not be decided with his proximity, and I leave it as my second alternative only.

responses.point: Kroll disclosed a possible perceived tie to John Hall's laboratory, with which Jun Ye is associated, and the chair's summary raises whether this should be recorded as a recusal question for B013.
responses.response: I appreciate that Kroll raised this himself, and I think the committee should record it. I do not think it changes the substance, because he describes it as not a documented conflict and the case for B013 rests on physics that every member ranked. Of the eight openings, seven placed it in the top three and Danielsson, Johansson and I ranked it second and Olsson and Pearce third, so the support does not depend on his vote. If he were to recuse himself, I would still vote the same way. I would add that a recorded disclosure is better than a later objection.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B013 explicitly for its defensible attribution, not because it exceeds the Higgs observation in significance, and flags that the omission of the Paris, German and NIST/JILA contributors needs wording in the citation.
responses.response: I agree with her distinction and I am in the same position: I rank B013 first for attribution, maturity and independence of the support, not because the clocks are the bigger result. I would go a little further on the citation. If we name the invention of the lattice and its realization at the 1e-18 level, then the Paris, German and NIST contributions are described as the confirmation that makes the realization secure rather than as omitted discoveries. I would not accept wording that implies the lattice clock is the only route to this accuracy, since the Al+ ion clock is a parallel one.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers the Higgs discovery with Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee, but regards the optical lattice clock as a fallback and says that attribution is the real weakness of the Higgs case.
responses.response: His own case against B001 states the problem more clearly than I could: any three names will look arbitrary to part of the community, and a cleaner two-person structure should be preferred to adjudicating a collaboration-scale dispute. On the other side, his objection that overlap with 2005 and 2012 weakens B013 is the one I take most seriously. I think the citation answers it, because the comb made optical frequencies countable and the lattice solved the separate problem of interrogating many atoms without Stark shifts. If he thinks that distinction does not hold, I would like to hear which part of the physics fails, since otherwise I regard his fallback as already giving B013 the majority.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that optical lattice clocks are distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, which depends on the wording of the citation.
Whether the redefinition of the second will happen, or be firmly scheduled, by the time of the decision; I do not think it is decisive but I cannot exclude that it will be read as such.
How the credit between Katori's concept and Ye's performance advances, and the contributions of Lemonde, Takamoto, the PTB groups and the JILA team, should be reflected.
Whether the Higgs supporters can agree on one defensible trio and a stated principle; my attribution concern about B001 could be answered by that, and my preference would then be open to change.
My recollection of dates and individual roles comes from general knowledge and is not verified against primary sources.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent from my provided profile: none of the credited names for B013, B001 or B054 is a documented co-author, supervisor or colleague, and my work on turbulence, random matrices and neural networks does not overlap with these fields. I note Kroll's disclosed Hall-laboratory tie and Johansson's WACQT link as their own flags; my vote on B013 does not depend on either member.
